html:
An earthquake that struck Antioch in Syria in late May 526, followed by a fire that burned for days. About 250,000 people are said to have died, which would make it one of the deadliest earthquakes in history.

Antioch was one of the largest cities of the Eastern Roman Empire, and the city was full of visitors for a church feast when the quake came. The chronicler John Malalas, who came from Antioch, describes buildings falling and fire spreading from the ruins. The patriarch Euphrasius was among the dead.

Emperor Justin I sent money to rebuild, and his nephew Justinian continued the work. Another strong quake hit in 528, after which the city was renamed Theoupolis, "City of God". Then in 540 the Persian shah Khosrow I sacked Antioch and carried off its people. The city never regained its old size. The same fault zone struck again in the 2023 Turkey and Syria earthquakes.
